suggestedPolicy.description: The suggested org policy that replaces the applied policy.

appliedPolicy.description: The org policy currently applied on the assured workload resource.

GoogleCloudAssuredworkloadsV1WorkloadUpd.description: A workload update is a change to the workload's compliance configuration.

createTime.description: The time the update was created.

state.description: Output only. The state of the update.
enumDescriptions: Unspecified.
The update is available to be applied.
The update has been applied.
The update has been withdrawn by the service.

name.description: Output only. Immutable. Identifier. Resource name of the WorkloadUpdate. Format: organizations/{organization}/locations/{location}/workloads/{workload}/updates/{update}

updateTime.description: The time the update was last updated.

GoogleCloudAssuredworkloadsV1ViolationRe.description: Remediation guidance to resolve a compliance violation.

compliantValues.description: The values that can resolve the violation. For example, for list organization policy violations, this field contains the list of allowed or denied values.

remediationType.description: Output only. The remediation type, which is based on the type of organization policy values that were violated.
enumDescriptions: Default value. The remediation type isn't specified.
Remediation for a boolean organization policy violation.
Remediation for a list organization policy violation where the monitoring rule specifies allowed values.
Remediation for a list organization policy violation where the monitoring rule specifies denied values.
Remediation for a `gcp.restrictCmekCryptoKeyProjects` organization policy violation.
Remediation for a resource violation.
Remediation for a resource violation that's caused by the `gcp.restrictNonCmekServices` organization policy.

instructions.description: Required. The instructions to resolve the violation.

consoleInstructions.description: Instructions to resolve the violation by using the Google Cloud console.

gcloudInstructions.description: Instructions to resolve the violation by using the gcloud CLI.

partnerPermissions.description: Required. The partner permissions to be updated.

updateMask.description: Required. The list of fields to be updated. E.g. update_mask { paths: "partner_permissions.data_logs_viewer"}

etag.description: Optional. The etag of the workload. If this is provided, it must match the server's etag.

GoogleCloudAssuredworkloadsV1MutatePartn.description: Request for updating permission settings for a partner workload.

GoogleCloudAssuredworkloadsV1ViolationRe.description: Instructions to remediate a violation by using the Google Cloud console.

additionalLinks.description: Additional URLs with more information about the steps.

consoleUris.description: Links to the Google Cloud console pages where the violation can be resolved.

steps.description: The steps to resolve the violation by using the Google Cloud console.

orgPolicyConstraint.description: Output only. Immutable. Deprecated: This field is deprecated and might be removed in a future version of the API. Use `non_compliant_org_policy` instead, which contains the full resource name of the organization policy, including the constraint name. The organization policy constraint that was changed in a non-compliant way, which resulted in this violation.

auditLogLink.description: Output only. Immutable. A link to the Cloud Audit Logs entries for the violated resource. Format: `https://console.cloud.google.com/logs/query;query={logName}{protoPayload.resourceName}{timeRange}{folder}`

nonCompliantOrgPolicy.description: Output only. Immutable. The name of the organization policy that was modified with a non-compliant change and resulted in this violation. Formats: * `projects/{project_number}/policies/{constraint_name}` * `folders/{folder_id}/policies/{constraint_name}` * `organizations/{organization_id}/policies/{constraint_name}`

resourceName.description: Optional. Output only. For resource violations, the full resource name of the non-compliant resource. For example, `//storage.googleapis.com/myprojectxyz-testbucket`. This field is empty for organization policy violations.

parentProjectNumber.description: Optional. Output only. For resource violations, the number of the project that contains the non-compliant resource. This field is empty for organization policy violations.

childResourceViolationCount.description: Optional. Output only. For organization policy violations, the number of resource violations that are associated with this violation. This field is `0` for resource violations.

updateTime.description: Output only. The time when the violation record was last updated.

acknowledged.description: Whether the violation has been acknowledged.

category.description: Output only. The category that the violation is mapped to. For example, `Location`, `Service Usage`, `Access`, or `Encryption`.

acknowledgementTime.description: Optional. The time when the violation was first acknowledged. To find the most recent time that the violation was acknowledged, check `exception_contexts`. This field is absent when `acknowledged` is `false`.

state.description: Output only. The state of the violation.
enumDescriptions: Default value. The state isn't specified.
The violation is resolved.
The violation is unresolved and hasn't been acknowledged.
The violation is unresolved and has been acknowledged as an exception.

exceptionContexts.description: Output only. The details of all of the acknowledgements (exceptions) for the violation.

associatedOrgPolicyViolationId.description: Optional. Output only. For resource violations, the ID of the organization policy violation that caused this resource violation. This field is empty for organization policy violations.

beginTime.description: Output only. The time of the event that triggered the violation.

description.description: Output only. A description of the violation. For example, `OrgPolicy gcp.resourceLocations has non compliant value.`

exceptionAuditLogLink.description: Output only. Immutable. A link to the Cloud Audit Logs entries that contain the business justification that was provided when the violation was acknowledged. Format: `https://console.cloud.google.com/logs/query;query={logName}{protoPayload.resourceName}{protoPayload.methodName}{timeRange}{organization}`

remediationMarkdown.description: Output only. The remediation instructions for the violation, in Markdown format. This field is only populated by `GetViolation` when using `VIOLATION_VIEW_DATA_BOUNDARY`. When this field isn't populated, see `remediation` instead.

name.description: Output only. Immutable. The resource name of the violation. Format: `organizations/{organization}/locations/{location}/workloads/{workload_id}/violations/{violations_id}`

resolveTime.description: Output only. The time of the event that resolved the violation. This field is empty if the violation is unresolved.

remediation.description: Output only. The remediation guidance for the violation.

violationType.description: Output only. The type of the violation.
enumDescriptions: Default value. The violation type isn't specified.
A violation that's caused by a non-compliant change to an organization policy.
A violation that's caused by a non-compliant resource.

resourceType.description: Optional. Output only. For resource violations, the type of the non-compliant resource. For example, `compute.googleapis.com/Disk`. This field is empty for organization policy violations.

affectedFrameworks.description: Output only. The IDs of the compliance frameworks that are affected by this violation. For example, `builtin-fedramp-high`. This field is only populated when using `VIOLATION_VIEW_DATA_BOUNDARY`.

GoogleCloudAssuredworkloadsV1Violation.description: A compliance violation that's detected by Assured Workloads monitoring. A violation is created when an organization policy or a resource in a workload (or a Data Boundary scope) changes in a way that doesn't comply with the controls of the applicable compliance regime or framework.

GoogleCloudAssuredworkloadsV1OrgPolicy.description: This assured workload service object is used to represent the org policy attached to a resource. It servces the same purpose as the orgpolicy.v2.Policy object but with functionality that is limited to what is supported by Assured Workloads(e.g. only one rule under one OrgPolicy object, no conditions, etc).

constraint.description: The constraint name of the OrgPolicy. e.g. "constraints/gcp.resourceLocations".

reset.description: Ignores policies set above this resource and restores to the `constraint_default` value. `reset` can only be true when `rules` is empty and `inherit` is false.

inherit.description: If `inherit` is true, policy rules of the lowest ancestor in the resource hierarchy chain are inherited. If it is false, policy rules are not inherited.

resource.description: Resource that the OrgPolicy attaches to. Format: folders/123" projects/123".

additionalLinks.description: Additional URLs with more information about the steps.

GoogleCloudAssuredworkloadsV1AssetMoveAn.description: Represents move analysis results for an asset.

asset.description: The full resource name of the asset being analyzed. Example: //compute.googleapis.com/projects/my_project_123/zones/zone1/instances/instance1

assetType.description: Type of the asset being analyzed. Possible values will be among the ones listed [here](https://cloud.google.com/asset-inventory/docs/supported-asset-types).

analysisGroups.description: List of eligible analyses performed for the asset.

workloads.description: List of Workloads under a given parent.

nextPageToken.description: The next page token. Return empty if reached the last page.

additionalProperties.description: Properties of the object. Contains field @type with type URL.

details.description: A list of messages that carry the error details. There is a common set of message types for APIs to use.

code.description: The status code, which should be an enum value of google.rpc.Code.

message.description: A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the google.rpc.Status.details field, or localized by the client.

GoogleRpcStatus.description: The `Status` type defines a logical error model that is suitable for different programming environments, including REST APIs and RPC APIs. It is used by [gRPC](https://github.com/grpc). Each `Status` message contains three pieces of data: error code, error message, and error details. You can find out more about this error model and how to work with it in the [API Design Guide](https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors).

warnings.description: List of warnings. These are risks that may or may not result in compliance violations.

blockers.description: List of blockers. If not resolved, these will result in compliance violations in the target.

GoogleCloudAssuredworkloadsV1MoveAnalysi.description: Represents the successful move analysis results for a group.

GoogleCloudAssuredworkloadsV1MoveAnalysi.description: Represents a logical group of checks performed for an asset. If successful, the group contains the analysis result, otherwise it contains an error with the failure reason.

totalSize.description: The total number of violations that match the request, across all pages. This field might not be populated for all requests; when it's not populated, its value is `0`.

nextPageToken.description: A token that can be sent as `page_token` to retrieve the next page. If this field is empty, there are no subsequent pages.

activeViolationCount.description: Number of current orgPolicy violations which are not acknowledged.

get.description: Retrieves an Assured Workloads violation by its resource name.

name.description: Required. The resource name of the violation to retrieve (that is, the value of `Violation.name`). Format: `organizations/{organization}/locations/{location}/workloads/{workload}/violations/{violation}`

enumDescriptions: Defaults to the ASSURED_WORKLOADS view.
Includes the basic metadata about the violation.
Includes all information about the violation, including details about the data boundary.
view.description: Optional. The violation view (`VIOLATION_VIEW_ASSURED_WORKLOADS` or `VIOLATION_VIEW_DATA_BOUNDARY`) that the violation belongs to. If not specified, `VIOLATION_VIEW_ASSURED_WORKLOADS` is used.

pageToken.description: Optional. A page token, received from a previous `ListViolations` call. Provide this token to retrieve the subsequent page. When paginating, all other parameters that are provided to `ListViolations` must match the call that provided the page token.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of violations to return. The service might return fewer violations than this value. If unspecified, at most 100 violations are returned. The maximum value is 1000; values above 1000 are coerced to 1000.

filter.description: Optional. A filter expression that restricts the violations that are returned. The syntax follows [AIP-160](https://google.aip.dev/160). Only the equality operator (`=`) is supported, and expressions can be combined with `AND`, `OR`, and `NOT`. When `view` is `VIOLATION_VIEW_DATA_BOUNDARY`, the following fields are supported: `violationId`, `category`, `state` (`UNRESOLVED`, `RESOLVED`, or `EXCEPTION`), `violationType` (`ORG_POLICY` or `RESOURCE`), `resourceType`, `resourceName`, `project`, `associatedOrgPolicyViolationId`, `cloudControlName`, `workloadDisplayName`, and `complianceType` (a framework ID). Example: `state = "UNRESOLVED" AND complianceType = "builtin-fedramp-high"`

orderBy.description: Optional. A comma-separated list of fields to sort the results by. The default sort order is ascending; to sort in descending order, append ` desc` to the field name. For example, `update_time desc,category`. When `view` is `VIOLATION_VIEW_DATA_BOUNDARY`, the following fields are supported: `begin_time`, `update_time`, `resource_type`, `state`, and `category`. If not specified, results are sorted by `begin_time` in descending order.

When `view` is `VIOLATION_VIEW_DATA_BOUNDARY`, violations are listed for the entire organization and location, and the workload ID is ignored. Format: `organizations/{organization}/locations/{location}/workloads/{workload}`

view.description: Optional. The violation view (`VIOLATION_VIEW_ASSURED_WORKLOADS` or `VIOLATION_VIEW_DATA_BOUNDARY`) to list violations for. If not specified, `VIOLATION_VIEW_ASSURED_WORKLOADS` is used.

The caller must have `resourcemanager.folders.getIamPolicy` and `resourcemanager.folders.setIamPolicy` permissions on the assured workload folder.

pageSize.description: Optional. Page size. If a value is not specified, the default value of 10 is used. The maximum value is 50.

target.description: Required. The resource name of the folder-based destination workload. This workload is where the source resource will hypothetically be moved to. Specify the workload's relative resource name, formatted as: "organizations/{ORGANIZATION_ID}/locations/{LOCATION_ID}/workloads/{WORKLOAD_ID}" For example: "organizations/123/locations/us-east1/workloads/assured-workload-2"

pageToken.description: Optional. The page token from the previous response. It needs to be passed in the second and following requests.

project.description: The source type is a project. Specify the project's relative resource name, formatted as either a project number or a project ID: "projects/{PROJECT_NUMBER}" or "projects/{PROJECT_ID}" For example: "projects/951040570662" when specifying a project number, or "projects/my-project-123" when specifying a project ID.

analyzeWorkloadMove.description: Analyzes a hypothetical move of a source resource to a target workload to surface compliance risks. The analysis is best effort and is not guaranteed to be exhaustive.
